In [[cryptography]], '''Square''' (sometimes written '''S<small>QUARE</small>''')  is a [[block cipher]] invented by [[Joan Daemen]] and [[Vincent Rijmen]]. The design, published in 1997, is a forerunner to [[Rijndael]], which has been adopted as the [[Advanced Encryption Standard]]. Square was introduced together with a new form of [[cryptanalysis]] discovered by [[Lars Ramkilde Knudsen|Lars Knudsen]], called the "[[Square attack]]".

The structure of Square is a [[substitution–permutation network]] with eight rounds, operating on 128-bit blocks and using a 128-bit [[key (cryptography)|key]].

Square is not patented.
